bugs.description: Division by zero: no validation of denominator before division.
Hardcoded SECRET_KEY and API_KEY in source code.
SQL injection vulnerability: f-string used in SQL query.
ZeroDivisionError when empty list passed to average().
Discount over 100% produces negative price — no upper bound check.
Non-descriptive function name 'fn1' — violates naming conventions.
Possible SQL injection vector through string-based query construction.

Consider possible security implications associated with the subprocess module.

root_cause_analysis.root_cause: The function performs division without validating the denominator. When the denominator is zero, Python raises a ZeroDivisionError which is not caught, causing the application to crash.
root_cause_analysis.fix_suggestion: Add a guard clause before division: if b == 0: raise ValueError('Denominator cannot be zero')
root_cause_analysis.business_impact: Any calculation involving division by zero will crash the application, potentially causing data loss or service disruption.
root_cause_analysis.technical_impact: Unhandled ZeroDivisionError propagates up the call stack.
